# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-33 (Extended v218)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring/summer Year 9. Key Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Champs-Élysées, Rue Saint-Honoré, Luxembourg Garden, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Temple, sewers (Sainte-Avoye, Louvre, Montmartre, belt, Amelot, Beautreillis), Marais, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons, Saint-Paul church, Rue Beautreillis near Arsenal, Grand Sewer, Rue de l'Hôpital. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Wilholt, Torton, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Gulhaven.

## English Subplot Summary

**Established facts through Year 9**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford. Multiple residents migrated between villages: Taric Corrley (Staveford to Dungate), Marald Corrford and Fenelle (Dunstead to Salcombe/Ravenmere), Ismira Stenson (Dungate to Elmhaven winter Year 6, then Staveford autumn Year 8, finally Kelmere late spring/early summer Year 9), Matho Stenson (Elmhaven to Staveford winter Year 7, then Kelmere with Ismira summer Year 9), Elra Corrford (Elmhaven to Gulhaven), Islan and Vesmira Thornmere (Ostcombe to Dungate autumn Year 7; Islan died at Dungate of old age), Zavus Prydenridge (apprenticed, became ferryman summer Year 7), Gadrek Prydenridge (quit milling, took brewery work autumn Year 7; married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter at Ostcombe), Havie Prydenridge (married Isric Thornmere at Ostcombe; Havie never kept promise to Gadrek regarding old debt), Luvie Prydenridge (married Semor at Ostcombe; gave up weaving, took chandler work autumn Year 8), Tatho Brackick and Yewyn Haskick (Salcombe to Wilholt late Year 8), Ilrald Prydenridge (married eldest daughter of Rorald Lindmere at Torton in spring/summer Year 9), **Movie Prydenridge moved to Elmhaven.** **Vesmira Thornmere married Rimor Corrford in chapel at Dungate; couple lived in Dungate.**

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7). Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair chapel roof at Kelmere (winter Year 8). Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Kassa's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe.

**Property transfers**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards (fairly, kept it). Kassa gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8). Kassa gave bone compass to Ismira (autumn Year 8). Volan Stenworth pressed amber map into Rimor Corrford's hands, would take nothing for it. Gadrek Prydenridge won copper chalice from Yera Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it (winter Year 8). Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely.

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (confirmed Wenelle Lindmere to Rovus Prydenridge, winter Year 8).

**Chapter 33 domestic observations (spring/summer Year 9)**: Pelde Stenson and Pelde Stenworth both tired. Dalis Stenworth and Davus both tired. Rimor Corrford, Kassa Brackick, and Volan Stenworth complained of aching backs. Children chased hoop shrieking. Road all ruts and puddles. Frost silvered hedges. Bells rang thinly. Salt prices discussed as scandalous. Rimor hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Rimor and Kassa talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Volan laughed at story nobody else found funny. Kassa counted coins twice, came up penny short. Baker's boy late. Rain threatened but held off. Luvie Prydenridge bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Lurald told Istho they looked tired. Yera Stenworth spent evening sorting old letters. Lurald remarked river up; Yera said it always was in spring. Luvie told Rozek Stenenridge old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. Luvie and Semor Brackick argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Istho Stenworth hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. **Yera hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Only son of Luena Stenenridge packed single trunk and moved from Ostcombe to Elmhaven. Istho Stenworth counted coins twice, came up penny short. Nerine Prydenridge watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly. Jotho watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly. Luvie Prydenridge hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Jotho mended torn sleeve by window, said little. Yera Stenworth read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Rozek Stenenridge fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Istho Stenworth asked if it would rain; Isric only shrugged. Rozek and Luvie Prydenridge discussed salt prices as scandal. Smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps.**

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship, Revelation, Marriage, Aftermath, and Crisis

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed orphan, lawyer, father colonel-hero. Cosette revealed raised at convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (June)**: Éponine died leading Marius to barricade, gave letter from Cosette. Marius witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery**: Bullet deflected by pocket-book. Serious laceration, dislocated collar-bone from underground journey. **7 September**: Doctor declared recovery assured. When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette to him.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; another Fauchelevent was real father. **Dowry: five hundred eighty thousand francs, constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.** Gillenormand overwhelmed her with gifts: robes, lace, parures, ivory boxes, furnished chamber with elegant trifles.

**Wedding ceremony (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. Exchanged vows, signed registers, exchanged rings, knelt under white moire pall. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent injured hand paining him; begged excuse; would come tomorrow. Jean Valjean rose, gained antechamber unperceived, left during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis post-wedding**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets, pillow without case. All Cosette's feminine objects carried away. Only Jean Valjean's bed made up. Questioned: Should he force himself on happiness? Should he remain sort of father, half seen but respected? Should he present himself as though he had right? Should he bring past to future? Remained twelve long hours of winter night, ice-cold, motionless as corpse. Then shuddered convulsively, kissed Cosette's garments.

## Javert's Death

**Moral transformation**: Javert's certainty crumbled when confronted by Valjean's benevolent nature. All axioms crumbled. Loss of certainty caused supreme anguish.

**Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed on quay edge. Tall black figure appeared erect on parapet, bent towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down. Dull splash followed. Javert drowned.

## Jean Valjean's Revelation, Decline, and Estrangement

**Revelation (17 February morning after wedding)**: Very pale, eyes hollow, sunken by sleeplessness. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Justified: conscience implacable; duty places one in hell where God beside you. Entered engagements with himself; keeps them. Revealed situation himself—nothing forced him. If police arrived, exposed through own act, not another's. Chose danger over false name security.

**Marius's shock and rationalization**: Marius stood with mouth wide open. Pleaded with Jean Valjean not to tell Cosette: "She does not know, it would terrify her. What, a convict!" Jean Valjean seized with convulsion, tears inundating face. Marius later reflected: questioned whether failed in divining Jean Valjean's nature. Admitted chimerical, visionary side. Recalled during six-seven ecstatic weeks in Rue Plumet, never spoke to Cosette of Gorbeau hovel drama or Thénardiers. Accounted for this: benumbed state, intoxication with love, vague dull instinct to conceal. Concluded: even had discovered Jean Valjean convict, would not have changed him or Cosette. Nothing to regret. All was well.

**Marius's doubt about Javert (RUMOR—UNCONFIRMED)**: Recalled Jean Valjean in barricade but did not fight. Had he gone to revenge himself on Javert? Heard behind Rue Mondétour frightful pistol shot. Obvious hatred between police spy and galley-slave. **Jean Valjean had killed Javert. At least, seemed evident.** [RUMOR—Marius has not verified.]

**Marius's metaphysical rationalization**: God visible in affair. Jean Valjean horrible workman but admirable work. Dung-heap aids spring to create rose. Adored Cosette, possessed Cosette, Cosette splendidly pure. What enlightenment needed? Cosette light. Henceforth Marius to fulfill Providence's part to Cosette. Cosette left behind empty chrysalis: Jean Valjean.

**Marius's final conflicted position**: Man was convict—being without place in social ladder. Convict appeared hideous, repulsive. Not examined right man takes to dispose of irrevocable. Not shocked by vengeance. Weakness led to imprudent concession; promised Jean Valjean; must keep word. First duty to Cosette.

**Marius's investigation and moral uncertainty**: Acquired mysterious information about six hundred thousand francs without seeking it. Unable to probe out of respect for promised secret. Believed he had grave duty: restitution of money to someone sought with all possible discretion. In meanwhile, abstained from touching money.

**Cosette's alienation from Jean Valjean**: Address as _thou_ replaced by _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean," rendering him another person. She became more gay, less tender. Still loved him sincerely. One day chanced to say "father" to him. Flash of joy illuminated Jean Valjean's melancholy countenance. He caught her up: "Say Jean."—"Ah! truly, Monsieur Jean," she replied with laughter. "That is right," said he. Turned aside to wipe eyes. **This was the last time.** Complete extinction ensued. No more familiarity, no more good-morning with kiss. After losing Cosette wholly in one day, afterwards obliged to lose her again in detail.

**Marius's estrangement strategy**: Before marriage, put no questions to M. Fauchelevent; since that time, feared to put any to Jean Valjean. Regretted promise. Confined himself to gradually estranging Jean Valjean from house and effacing him from Cosette's mind. Always placed himself between them. More than effacement, it was eclipse.

**Cosette's magnetism**: Existed between Marius and Cosette all-powerful magnetism causing her to do, instinctively and mechanically, what Marius wished. Conscious of Marius' will in direction of "Monsieur Jean," she conformed to it. Husband had not been obliged to say anything; she yielded to vague but clear pressure of his tacit intentions. Her obedience consisted in not remembering what Marius forgot. Her soul had become so wholly her husband's that which was shrouded in gloom in Marius' mind became overcast in hers. However, concerning Jean Valjean, this forgetfulness was merely superficial. Rather heedless than forgetful. At bottom, sincerely attached to man whom so long called her father; but loved her husband still more dearly. This had somewhat disturbed balance of her heart, which leaned to one side only.

**Jean Valjean's withdrawal pattern (late spring/summer 1833)**: Noticed old man neatly clad in black emerged daily at same hour towards nightfall from Rue de l'Homme Armé. Passed Blancs-Manteaux, gained Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, reached Rue de l'Écharpe, turned left into Rue Saint-Louis. Soon went only as far as Rue Pavée, shook head, turned back. Then did not overstep Blancs-Manteaux. Pendulum no longer wound up, oscillations growing shorter. Whole countenance expressed single idea: What is use? Eye dim, no radiance. Tears exhausted. Old man's head craned forward; chin moved; folds in gaunt neck painful to behold. Sometimes had umbrella under arm but never opened it.

**Physical deterioration**: **A week passed, Jean Valjean had not taken a step in his room. He still remained in bed.** Portress said to husband: "The good man upstairs does not get up, no longer eats, will not last long. That man has his sorrows. His daughter has made a bad marriage." One evening found difficulty raising himself on elbow; felt wrist, could not find pulse; breath short, halted at times; recognized he was weaker than ever before. Made effort, drew himself up into sitting posture, dressed himself in old workingman's clothes. Obliged to pause many times while dressing; putting arms through waistcoat made perspiration trickle from forehead. **One day descended staircase, took three steps in street, seated himself on post where Gavroche had found him meditating; remained there few moments, went upstairs again. This was the last oscillation of the pendulum. On following day he did not leave apartment. On day after that, he did not leave bed.**

**Preparations for death**: Took Bishop's candlesticks from chimney-piece, took two wax candles from drawer, put them in candlesticks. Lighted them though broad daylight, summer time. Every step exhausted him; obliged to sit down. Not ordinary fatigue which expends strength to renew it; remnant of all movement possible to him; life drained which flows away drop by drop. Chair placed in front of mirror, so fatal for him, so providential for Marius. **He was eighty years old; before Marius' marriage, would have hardly been taken for fifty; that year had counted for thirty. What he bore on brow was no longer wrinkles of age, but mysterious mark of death. Hollowing of that pitiless nail could be felt there. Cheeks pendulous; skin of face had color leading one to think earth already upon it; corners of mouth drooped as in mask ancients sculptured on tombs. Gazed into space with air of reproach; one would have said he was grand tragic being who had cause to complain of someone.**

**Writing attempt**: Forced to rise and put few drops of water in ink. Compelled to write with back of pen. Wiped brow from time to time. **Exclaimed within himself [lamentable cries heard by God alone]: "All is over. I shall never see her more. She is a smile which passed over me. I am about to plunge into night without even seeing her again. Oh! one minute, one instant, to hear her voice, to touch her dress, to gaze upon her, the angel! and then to die! What is frightful is to die without seeing her. She would smile on me, she would say a word to me, would that do any harm to any one? No, all is over, and forever. Here I am all alone. My God! My God! I shall never see her again!"**

## Thénardier's Blackmail Attempt

**Thénardier's discovery and visit**: Through daughter Azelma tracking married pair since 16 February, and personal researches, Thénardier discovered Cosette was Madame la Baronne Pontmercy. Through induction, discovered man encountered in Grand Sewer. Knew Cosette's identity but meant to be discreet. Caught inkling of her illegitimacy but judged this insufficient leverage for sale; had better wares. Feared revealing bastard status would only result in being kicked out. Wore black cloth coat, black wool trousers, silk waistcoat, boots, linen, green glasses with double screen, hair plastered flat, gray hair, hat in hand, bent attitude, bunch of seals from fob. Claimed possession of secret concerning individual in Marius' family. **Offered to drive individual from family who has no right there, as Madame la Baronne being of lofty birth; sanctuary of virtue cannot cohabit longer with crime without abdicating.** Demanded twenty thousand francs for secret. Marius replied with cold tone and double reply of "I know it," laconicism not favorable to dialogue.

**Thénardier's exposure and Marius's revelation**: With agility of monkey, Thénardier tore off spectacles, withdrew two quills from nose by sleight of hand, took off face as man takes off hat. **Thénardier strangely surprised; would have been troubled, had he capable of such a thing. He had come to bring astonishment, and it was he who had received it. This humiliation worth five hundred francs to him, accepted it; but bewildered nonetheless.** Beheld Baron Pontmercy for first time; despite disguise, Baron recognized him thoroughly. Thénardier never seen Marius before, had heard daughters vaguely speak of poor young man named Marius who lived in house. Had written letter to him without knowing him.

**Marius's knowledge and counterattack**: **Marius revealed Javert's suicide facts**: Announced two newspapers: _Moniteur_ of 15th of June, 1832, announced Javert's suicide, adding that Javert reported to prefect that, having been taken prisoner in barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie, he owed his life to magnanimity of insurgent who, holding him under pistol, fired into air instead of blowing out his brains. **Marius possessed evidence, certain date, irrefragable proof. Could not doubt.** Marius felt humiliated that colonel-hero should have owed anything to Thénardier. Thénardier's letter of change drawn from tomb by Marius' father, protested up to that day. Seemed occasion to avenge Colonel for misfortune of being saved by rascal. Marius was content—about to deliver Colonel's shade from unworthy creditor, rescue father's memory from debtors' prison. By side of this duty lay another: to elucidate, if possible, source of Cosette's fortune.

**Marius's confrontation speech**: **Told Thénardier: "You are an infamous wretch! you are a liar, a calumniator, a villain. You came to accuse that man, you have only justified him; you wanted to ruin him, you have only succeeded in glorifying him. And it is you who are the thief! And it is you who are the assassin! I saw you, Thénardier Jondrette, in that lair on the Rue de l'Hôpital. I know enough about you to send you to the galleys and even further if I choose. Here are a thousand francs, bully that you are! Of a Colonel! I wouldn't give a ha'penny for a general. And you come here to commit infamies! I tell you that you have committed all crimes. Go! disappear! Only be happy, that is all that I desire. Ah! monster! here are three thousand francs more. Take them. You will depart to-morrow, for America, with your daughter; for your wife is dead, you abominable liar. I shall watch over your departure, you ruffian, and at that moment I will count out to you twenty thousand francs. Go get yourself hung elsewhere!"**

**Thénardier's outcome (FACT—Established)**: **The moral wretchedness of Thénardier, bourgeois who missed his vocation, was irremediable. He was in America what he had been in Europe. Contact with evil man sometimes suffices to corrupt good action and cause evil things to spring from it. With Marius' money, Thénardier set up as slave-dealer.**
